title: Etale/pro-etale comparison respects the canonical open tensor map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on small representatives of the ordinary etale and pro-etale sites in a common larger universe, with the unbounded derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact derived comparison pullback [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Let $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $N\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ be arbitrary. Write
$$e_F:A_Xj^{e}_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{p}_!A_UF$$
for the degreewise derived comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], using exact extensions by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Superscripts $e,p$ distinguish the two sites. Let $t_T:A_T(F\otimes^L G)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_TF\otimes^L A_TG$ be the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and let $a_j:A_Uj_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_p^*A_X$ be the canonical derived pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Define
$$h_{K,N}=(1\otimes a_{j,N})\circ t_U:
 A_U(K\otimes^Lj_e^*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_UK\otimes^Lj_p^*A_XN.$$
Let $\gamma^e_{K,N}:j^e_!K\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\sim}j^e_!(K\otimes^Lj_e^*N)$ and $\gamma^p_{A_UK,A_XN}$ be the canonical open tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor, lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula]. Then the following equality holds in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, naturally in $K,N$:
$$
j^p_!(h_{K,N})\circ e_{K\otimes^Lj_e^*N}\circ A_X(\gamma^e_{K,N})
=\gamma^p_{A_UK,A_XN}\circ(e_K\otimes1)\circ t_X,
$$
as maps from $A_X(j^e_!K\otimes^LN)$ to $j^p_!(A_UK\otimes^Lj_p^*A_XN)$. No boundedness, constructibility, properness, or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is required.

proof.text: The comparison pullback is exact, so its termwise action on complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms and identifies cohomology with the pulled-back cohomology. The extension-by-zero comparison is natural in the sheaf, and both étale and pro-étale extension by zero are exact. Therefore the degreewise maps e_F descend to natural isomorphisms on the unbounded derived categories, with no boundedness condition. The derived tensor comparison t_T is the canonical natural comparison supplied by the ringed-topos tensor-pullback lemma.

proof.text: On the étale site, the canonical map gamma^e is the natural open-tensor isomorphism for an open immersion, valid for arbitrary unbounded complexes. On the pro-étale site, the extension-zero projection-formula node gives the corresponding canonical isomorphism gamma^p. The generic open-tensor normalization records that this pro-étale map is the adjunction-normalized map: its inverse is the j_! dashv j^* adjunct of the open unit tensored with the identity, and after restricting to the open its component is the identity. Thus both gamma maps are fixed by the same unit/counit normalization rather than by an arbitrary choice of isomorphism.

The pullback comparison a_j is natural and compatible with identities and composites, and the tensor comparison t_U is natural in both variables. Consequently the composite h_{K,N}=(1 tensor a_{j,N}) composed with t_U is exactly the canonical comparison from A_U(K tensor^L j_e^*N) to A_UK tensor^L j_p^*A_XN. This identification uses the same restriction map j on the two sites and does not introduce a second pullback or tensor structure.

Choose flat-term K-flat representatives P of K and Q of N. The tensor-pullback comparison is represented termwise by the canonical pure-tensor map, while e is represented termwise by the natural sheaf comparison between the two extension-by-zero functors. Thus both composites are maps between the corresponding extension-by-zero tensor complexes. On each object of the localized site, the ordinary sheaf identity underlying the open tensor comparison sends a pure tensor x tensor y to the extension-by-zero section of x tensor the restriction of y; this identity is checked on the open restriction and on stalks at points of the complement, where both sides have zero stalk by the extension-by-zero prescriptions. The adjunction-normalized description in lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization makes the restriction maps the identity, and full faithfulness of j_! then identifies the resulting sheaf maps. Naturality with respect to the differentials gives equality of chain maps. K-flat descent and localization in the cited tensor-pullback lemma give the displayed equality in the unbounded derived category.

proof.text: Every comparison, tensorator, restriction comparison, extension-by-zero comparison, and open-tensor map used above is natural in K and N. Hence the componentwise equality is natural in both variables. The construction used only exactness, adjunction units and counits, and the canonical tensor comparisons, so it applies to arbitrary unbounded K and N and requires no boundedness, constructibility, properness, or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis.
